title: "4.9 Gate record"
order: 9
---

::: {.callout-important}
## The gate

**Held-out AUC ≥ {{< var score.gate >}}**, on the held-out {{< var score.test_share >}} of
all applicants ([4.2](data.qmd#split-and-seed)). Current value
{{< var score.auc_holdout >}}: **met**. KS is reported, not gated.
:::

## Where it is asserted

At the end of training, in `score/src/train.py`. A scorecard that misses the gate fails
its own training run:

```python
AUC_GATE = 0.78   # workshop gate — the committed promise (KS reported, not gated)
...
    assert auc >= AUC_GATE, f"GATE FAIL: AUC {auc:.4f} < {AUC_GATE}"
```

The value is also written into `score/models/metadata.json`, under `["gate"]["auc_min"]`.

## Where it is recomputed, independently

`verify.py` carries its own copy of the gate:

```python
SCORE_AUC_GATE = 0.78    # verify.py
```

and its scorecard check does not read the stored metric. It loads `scorecard.pkl`,
redraws the held-out split from the committed data with the platform seed, recomputes the
AUC and compares it with its own constant. On `main` it then recomputes every fact in this
chapter, including the gate as `score.src.train.AUC_GATE` reads it
([D9](../d9-implementation.qmd)).

This is why **a relaxed local gate cannot pass.** Lowering `AUC_GATE` in `train.py` lets a
weaker model finish training and save its artifacts, but `verify.py` recomputes that
model's AUC against the constant it carries itself, and fails. The gate lives in two
places on purpose: the training script is where a developer works, and the checker is
not.

## Why this value

The gate was set below the ceiling this data allows ([4.5](performance.qmd#the-ceiling)),
so that it is demanding but reachable. The committed scorecard meets it with its whole
bootstrap interval ({{< var score.auc_ci_lo >}} – {{< var score.auc_ci_hi >}}) above the
gate, and sits indistinguishable from the ceiling. A gate above the ceiling could be
passed only by leakage or by chance in the sample.

## What the gate does not cover

- **The booked population.** The gate is measured on all applicants; on the booked, the
  model scores {{< var score.pop.booked.auc >}}. Finding 2 ([4.7](limitations.qmd)) and the
  monitoring plan ([4.8](monitoring.qmd)) carry this.
- **Stress.** The bureau-feed-down refit fails the gate
  ([4.6](sensitivity.qmd#bureau-feed-down-a-gate-failure-documented)). That is a documented
  result about the model's dependence on its inputs, and it moves neither the gate nor the
  committed model.

## History

| Version | Change | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| `stage-2` (commit `99b201c`) | gate introduced with the scorecard, in `train.py` and `verify.py` | {{< var score.gate >}} |
| `stage-3` to `stage-5`, `v1.0` to `v1.4`, `main` | unchanged | {{< var score.gate >}} |

The gate has not changed since it was introduced, and it is never relaxed to let a model
pass ([D9](../d9-implementation.qmd#gates-are-hard-asserts-recomputed-independently)). A
change to it would be a change of the committed promise: made on `main`, recorded in a new
version tag, and shown in this table.
